Resolves #6858

`grid.plugin.AnimateRows` works again on the pooled grid body, for 13.3 (milestone v13.3, the operator's backlog call on 2026-10-15).

The plugin predated the Row pool (#8965). It mapped vdom rows by their pooled slot id and pushed new row vdom, so on `dev` at `7f0856c106` every header sort and every filter in `examples/grid/animatedRowSorting` threw `owner.createRow is not a function`. Its SCSS also gave every row a permanent `transition: transform`, so ordinary scroll recycling animated: the "global transform transitions" that [PooledGridAnimation.md](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/guides/datahandling/PooledGridAnimation.md) rejects.

The repair follows that guide's source contracts: movement is keyed by record identity, and the pool is never reordered, appended or removed.
- Before the body re-binds, the plugin notes the offset of each displayed record.
- `createViewData(true)` re-binds the pool silently. Each row then starts at its new record's previous offset, so the first update changes nothing on screen; a record that was not displayed starts transparent.
- The next update adds `neo-animate-rows-moving` with the new offsets. That class is the only one under which a row transitions, and `neo-is-scrolling` overrides it.
- A scroll, any next store event, a switch of row mode, a destroy or a failed first update between the two steps calls `settle()`. It puts the displaced rows where the body renders them (record-fenced and geometry-aware, as `Row#createVdom` places them), drops the class, and invalidates the pending second step. A failed first update is still reported, and one from a superseded change leaves the newer move alone.
- A load that is not a sort replaces the records, so it renders through the body as usual, after settling.

Related: #13219 (the pooled animation contract), #19772 (locked bodies ignore the grid's configs, found here), #19712 (the 13.3 notes, whose AnimateRows bound changes with this merge)

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real App Worker, the e2e engine tier) for the browser behaviour, plus L2 unit arms for the two steps and their interruptions → L3 required (row offsets and transitions are browser-observable).

## AC Evidence

The ticket is a 2025 one-liner, so its acceptance criteria come from [the intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/6858#issuecomment-6199457893), plus @neo-gpt's three fork boundaries (A2A, 18:50Z).

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No throw on sort and filter | `AnimatedRowSorting.spec.mjs`: the fixture fails any test whose page or worker logs an error; all three tests pass. |
| The final order | The Firstname sort, the `l` filter and the Lastname sort each settle every displayed record at `index × rowHeight`. |
| A mid-transition sample | A per-frame sampler follows a record by its Firstname cell: Amanda starts at `5 × rowHeight`, passes a value strictly between, and ends at 0; under the filter, Carol goes from `4 ×` to `2 ×` the same way. |
| No transform transition outside the window | "outside a sort or filter, the rows carry no transition": every row reads `transition-duration: 0s` before a sort and again once it settles. |
| Invert only after a real re-bind (fork 1) | The in-flight deferral falls back to a plain `createViewData()`. An early return binds nothing, so every row reads `from === rowIndex` and none moves. `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` › "the first step shows each record where it was…" pins the first step: Row 10 at its previous offset, Row 100 transparent, Row 1 unmoved. |
| Keep the pin offset (fork 2) | Every offset goes through `Row#getRowTransform`, which carries `--grid-row-pin-offset`. |
| Fence late callbacks (fork 3; review RA-1, RA-2) | `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs`: a scroll between the steps, a filter between them (one whose re-bind leaves Row 10's row untouched), a load that is not a sort, a switch to content-sized rows and a destroy each leave the rows settled, the class off and no error. A rejected first step settles its rows and is still reported; a late rejection of a superseded step leaves the newer move running. The first test also pins the pool: row ids, vdom reference order and count are unchanged. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The prescription.** The ticket (2025) asked for a record-keyed map inside the old mechanism. The June guide rejects that mechanism, so this repair moves the live rows. @neo-gpt, the guide's author, read the fork: this approach fits the flat-grid contract, with the three boundaries above.
- **A record that leaves the display does not fade out.** Its slot already shows another record. The guide keeps the snapshot overlay for TreeGrid, where collapsed children need exactly that.
- **Locked columns: #19772.** Locked bodies are built from `...me.body.initialConfig`, a property nothing assigns, so they never get `animatedRowSorting`, nor any other body or header-toolbar config. The locked-alignment test moves to that ticket.
- **Docs:** PooledGridAnimation.md now describes the repaired plugin in its *Source Contracts* row and its rejected-alternative paragraph. `AnimateRowsContentSized.spec.mjs` keeps its assertions; its wording now names `neo-animate-rows` as the class the transitions hang on.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first:** at `7f0856c106` the new e2e spec fails 3/3. Both movement tests throw `owner.createRow is not a function` and sample no in-between offset (Amanda stays at 160; Carol jumps 128 → 64), and the third reads 500 ms transitions on every row.
- **The fences can fail:** with `settle()`'s row placement disabled, "a scroll between the steps…" and "a store change between the steps…" go red, and the other three stay green. Against `c409cbf2de`'s plugin, the RA-1 and RA-2 regressions go red; the superseded-rejection control passes on both, as a control should.
- **Green at `a6a4627dad`, Playwright 1.64 / Chromium 156:** `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` 8/8 (`--repeat-each=3` → 24/24); unit suite 5198; the e2e grid specs 188. At `c409cbf2de`: `AnimatedRowSorting.spec.mjs` 3/3 (`--repeat-each=3` → 9/9); `AnimateRowsContentSized.spec.mjs` 6/6.
- **Full suites:** unit 5194 passed; components 450 + `MonacoEditor.spec.mjs` 9/9; e2e engine tier 274 passed, 3 skipped (the Brain-gated specs run in CI). Two reds were local environment, re-run to green: `browserLifecycleReporter.spec.mjs` failed while a probe ran concurrently, and passes 11/11 alone. The Monaco DOMPurify arm read the stale local bundle (DOMPurify 3.4.15 against npm's 3.4.16) and passes 9/9 after `npm run bundle-monaco`.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-10-15T19:40:56Z

**Author response to the review at `c409cbf2de`, both actions addressed at `a6a4627dad`.**

- **RA-1 (ordinary load between the steps): fixed.** `onStoreLoad` and `onStoreFilter` now call `settle()` before anything else, so a load that is not a sort reaches the body only after the displaced rows are placed and the pending second step is invalidated. The body's own handler keeps its force and chunk behaviour unchanged. Regression: `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` › "a load that is not a sort between the steps settles the rows, and the late second step changes nothing". It removes the offscreen Row 199 between the steps (a load without `isSort`), then asserts at once that Row 10 sits at its index-2 offset, nothing is transparent and the class is off, and asserts the same again past the transition, so there is no late rearm.
- **RA-2 (rejected first step): fixed.** The rejection branch settles when the rejection belongs to the current change (`change === me.#change`), and reports the failure either way, unless it is `Neo.isDestroyed`. Regressions: "a rejected first step settles the rows and still reports the failure", and the control "a late rejection of a superseded first step leaves the newer move alone": a newer sort's transition keeps running after the old step rejects, and the old failure is still reported.

**Red against the reviewed plugin:** with only `AnimateRows.mjs` reverted to `c409cbf2de`, the RA-1 and RA-2 regressions fail and the superseded-rejection control passes, as a control should.

**Green at `a6a4627dad`:** `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` 8/8 (`--repeat-each=3` → 24/24), the unit suite 5198 passed, and the e2e grid specs 188 passed. The PR body is updated to match.

On your `[TOOLING_GAP]`: right, the step units are bucket-B and skipped in the hosted unit job. They ran locally at this head, and the browser cases run in engine CI.
